text:
B: Hiya, can you hear me alright? I'm Craig, I'm up in Warrington.
A: Hi, yes, I can hear you. I'm Klára, in London. Walthamstow.
B: Lovely. I've seen the dinosaur on your sofa, so I'm guessing there's a little one about?
A: (laughs) Yes, my son, Matěj. He's three and a half. And I saw the drawing of a dog on your fridge.
B: That's Alfie's, he's six. That's our dog, Biscuit, apparently, although it looks more like a horse. Funny thing, I just had a call with a woman whose dog's called Biscuit as well. Same breed and everything.
A: Really? This is quite a coincidence.
B: I know, I thought it was a wind-up. So are you working, or at home with him?
A: At home, at the moment. Before, I worked in retail. A department store on Oxford Street, on the tills and the customer desk, until 2021.
B: Oh, customer desk. You'll have seen some things, then.
A: Yes. (laughs) People shouting about a receipt for a scarf, very angry. But I was quite good with it. I just let them talk, and then mostly they calm down.
B: Do you know what, that's half my job. I'm in sales, flooring for offices and schools and care homes, and honestly most of it's just letting a facilities manager moan at you for twenty minutes about his lino, and then he signs the order. You let people get it off their chest, you know.
A: Yes, exactly. Listening is the main thing.
B: So are you thinking of going back? Sorry, I'm being nosy.
A: No, it's okay. Yes, part-time, when he starts more hours at nursery. I'd like something like reception, maybe a school office. There's a short online course in office admin I looked at, but, erm, I haven't signed up yet.
B: Do it. Honestly. I left uni after a year, and I've done all my training through work since, and it's served me alright. Those little courses look good on a CV, you know.
A: Maybe I will. My husband says the same, but he doesn't say it so nicely.
B: (laughs) What does he do?
A: He's an electrician. Self-employed. At the moment he's doing a big rewiring job in Leyton, so he comes home very tired and falls asleep on the sofa at eight.
B: That's me as well, to be fair. I did three hundred-odd miles this week. I get in and Kerry's already done Alfie's tea and I've missed it, which, er, I don't love, if I'm honest.
A: It's hard. Tom also misses bedtime sometimes, and Matěj is very angry about it. He's three, so he tells you.
B: They don't hold back, do they? Alfie told me last week I smell like a car.
A: (laughs) Maybe he's right.
B: He probably is. Where are you from originally, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Brno, in Czech Republic. I came in 2014. I speak Czech with Matěj so he keeps the language.
B: That's brilliant, that. Two languages at three. Alfie can barely do one, he just says "Dad" in different tones.
